title: Reward-Model Disagreement as an Early-Warning Signal for Reward Hacking

original_idea.body:
# Reward-Model Disagreement as Early-Warning for Reward Hacking

**Problem:** Whether disagreement among multiple open reward models flags likely-hacked responses is untested.

**Direction:** Best-of-n against one target RM, score responses with a panel of other RMs, test whether inter-RM variance is higher for hacked responses. Report precision/recall.

**Why it matters:** A cheap disagreement detector for reward-hacked outputs. Pure inference.

**Relevant context:** RLHF Book over-optimization; arXiv:2606.03238.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Builds a detector for reward hacking, a core alignment failure; clear chain to monitoring infrastructure.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Best-of-n plus multi-RM scoring is inference-only; intermediate-to-guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused detector with precision/recall; depends on a hacked-vs-clean labeling proxy.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open RMs, pure inference; independent-friendly monitoring tool.

novelty.reasoning: RM ensembling reduces Goodharting is known; disagreement-as-detector framing may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Ensembling studied; disagreement-as-early-warning-signal angle may be open.
